headline: Saros holds the line, Predators win seven straight
text:
Nashville spent the first period getting outplayed in Las Vegas and the last ten minutes of regulation doing the outplaying, and somewhere in between Juuse Saros made sure none of it mattered. He stopped 40 of 42 shots, Roman Josi ended the fourth round of the shootout, and the Predators beat the Golden Knights 3-2 for their seventh straight win. Vegas's own run stops at four.

Ryan O'Reilly scored both Nashville goals, and neither came from a great look. The first, at 7:56 of the first period off Steven Stamkos and Mavrik Bourque, was an 18% chance. Vegas answered with the better hockey: Victor Olofsson cashed a rebound after Saros robbed Ivan Barbashev at the back door, and Rasmus Andersson walked into the slot alone in the second to make it 2-1. By expected goals, the quality of each team's chances, Vegas won the first period 1.64 to 0.81, and our win probability had the Golden Knights at 72% after Andersson's goal.

Then the third period flipped. Nashville out-chanced Vegas 1.07 to 0.53, and O'Reilly tied it at 9:44 with a wrister that had a 7% chance of going in, the swing goal of the night (our win chance for Nashville went from 18% to 48%). Adin Hill kept it there, including a stop on Alexander Kerfoot in the final minute, and finished 30 for 32. Markerzone wrote that a Tomas Hertl hit on Bourque drew O'Reilly's anger and could draw a look from Player Safety; that's worth watching, nothing more yet.

In the shootout, Trevor Connelly scored in the second round, Filip Forsberg answered in the third, and after Jack Eichel was stopped, Josi beat Hill. Over the full game, Vegas had the better of it: 3.71 expected goals to 3.26, and the Golden Knights deserved to win 57% of the time by our count. That gap was Saros, who saved 1.7 goals more than his shots deserved. A streak this long usually needs a night like this somewhere in it. The only other meeting, in October, went 5-2 to Vegas.
